newsitem.title: FRANCE: French, Saudi defence chiefs discuss partnership.
newsitem.headline: French, Saudi defence chiefs discuss partnership.

text.p: France and Saudi Arabia are discussing a reinforced defence and political partnership involving security in the Middle East, French Defence Minister Charles Millon said on Wednesday.
Millon told reporters he was discussing the partnership with Saudi Defence and Aviation Minister Prince Sultan on a three-day visit to France.
"We will enter into the subject of a partnership between Saudi Arabia and France in the defence field and other domains," Millon told a news briefing with the prince.
He said the partnership would involve "security and peace in the Near and Middle East."

"There will be repercussions in the fields of investment, judicial procedures and equipment but those are not the main reasons for the visit. First and foremost, we have political objectives," Millon said.
Both Millon and Sultan declined to talk about the possibility of specific arms sales.
Sultan said his country had embarked on a "policy of economic re-stabilisation" with the United States and Britain which would also be applied to France, probably with better formulas.

"We will see the birth of joint industries with French and Saudi capital. Capital and investments consolidate friendship between peoples. We hope to succeed in cooperation with France in all domains," he said.
Western diplomats in the Middle East said this week that the prince, who is also second deputy prime minister, was not expected to sign any military deals during the visit.
Paris is trying to convince Saudi Arabia to buy Leclerc main battle tanks made by France's Giat Industries, similar to those sold for $3.62 billion to the neighbouring United Arab Emirates in 1993.
Paris is competing with Britain and the United States for the major arms contract after its tanks were tested in the kingdom's desert this summer at Saudi Arabia's request.
Diplomats had said France also hoped to turn a memorandum of understanding on radar and surveillance systems for zone and border defence into contracts.
Prince Sultan, who visited Washington last week, is also to meet French President Jacques Chirac and Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
"The French government will receive him more as Saudi Arabia's second deputy prime minister than its defence minister," a French diplomat in the Middle East said.

He said military cooperation would be one of the many subjects that will be raised in the talks that will also cover regional developments including the situation in Iraq and the Arab-Israeli peace process.
But Paris, seeking to enhance its political role in the region, still hopes to promote military and commercial trade with the world's biggest arms purchaser.

France, which buys one-quarter of its oil from Saudi Arabia, is the kingdom's third biggest arms supplier after the United States and Britain. Weapons sales average $1.2 billion a year, roughly equivalent to civilian exports.
Chirac met Saudi King Fahd in Riyadh last July and both said their talks consolidated and ensured continued cooperation at all levels.
France took part in a U.S.-led Western military alliance that drove Iraqi troops out of Kuwait in the 1991 Gulf War.
